newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: SHORT-TERM MONEY RATES END WEEK MIXED.
newsitem.headline: SHORT-TERM MONEY RATES END WEEK MIXED.

text.p: HARARE, June 20 (Reutetr) - Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed in quiet Friday trade, dealers said.

The market opened with a Z$30 million shortage but liquidity was injected with the maturity of treasury bills and the central Reserve Bank auctioned Z$24 million worth of 91-day bills at a discount of 25 percent.
Treausury bills were also being traded on the secondary market at 24.4 percent from 24.5 percent on Thursday while call money was quoted unchanged at 22 percent.
Bankers acceptance bills were at 25.35 from 25.5 percent (buying) and at 25 percent from 24.5 percent (selling).
The buying rate quoted for 30-, 60- and 90-day NCD bills slipped to 25.5 from 26.5 from 26 percent, but they were being sold unchanged from Thursday's 25 percent.
